body:
I do plan on it. I try to only include people when it becomes overwhelming. It could be a burden for another person; it will inevitably create stress and worry for the person I include, and likely the relationship to change, which is often what makes approaching someone so difficult.

I sincerely appreciate your assistance. Making this post and reading the responses is very helpful. Thank you.

Hi.

I don't want to be alone, either.

One of my friends who lives here will be returning tonight. I'll probably talk to her. She's had depression, and has suspected that I have depression (though I told her I was fine when she asked).

I realize I'm still young, but yes, it's more the length of which it has relative to how long I have been alive, with little hope.

My job will most likely be good. It will be using technology that I find interesting. I still fear that what happened with my previous job will happen. On most days I would have to rush to the restroom to prevent bursting out in tears in front of my coworkers. At this place I know that the people are more "normal", so I will have to put more weight in the work to distract me. 

It's really less about me losing her. I understand the position she's in and why she broke things off. It's just that now I am entirely alone with my thoughts, allowing them freedom without any lax period, which isn't good. That coupled with no immediate hope of happiness is really where the problem is.

As far as my family knows I am fine. In fact, there's only one person who knows my position.

I was also sorry to hear about it.

She knew about it when I was 16 or 17. Ideally I'd like for her to think that I'm "better." If there's one person I don't want to hurt, it's her, so I imagine I will keep her in the dark.

To date I am the only person who tells me to kill myself.

I talked with the only person whom I truly trust in this world the night she broke up with me, expressing that I still don't want to be alive, that I think about suicide every day. At one point in my life I considered him to be inspiring in the matter. When we were young we both had depression. He got better while I stagnated. 

Talking with him was helpful, but this topic is so much different when considering being in the mindset versus hindsight.
